slides.headline: David was carved from a block nobody wanted
A rejected block
slides.text: Other sculptors had started on this marble and given up. It sat in the cathedral workshop for decades until a 26-year-old Michelangelo took it on in 1501.

slides.headline: Before the fight, not after
slides.text: Earlier Davids stand over Goliath's head. Michelangelo shows the tense moment before: furrowed brow, eyes fixed on the enemy.

slides.headline: Look at the eyes
slides.text: They don't point in quite the same direction. Seen from below and from the sides, the gaze still reads as focused.

slides.headline: The sling
slides.text: Over his left shoulder hangs the sling, running down his back. Easy to miss from the front.

slides.headline: Why is the hand so big?
slides.text: His right hand, holding the stone, is oversized. The statue was meant to be seen high up on the cathedral, so the proportions were adjusted.

slides.headline: Over 5 metres of marble
slides.text: Instead of the cathedral, it was placed in front of Palazzo Vecchio in 1504, a symbol of Florence standing up to stronger enemies.

slides.headline: It has been broken
slides.text: In 1527, during a riot, a bench thrown from the palace broke its left arm into pieces. They were collected and reattached.

slides.headline: Indoors since 1873
slides.text: The original was moved into the Accademia to protect it. In 1991 a man attacked its foot with a hammer. The David in the square today is a copy.
